The Prophet prostrated on reciting An-Najm, with all present but an old man who lifted earth to his forehead, and at Sad, yet not when Zaid recited An-Najm.
Abu Huraira prostrated at Al-Inshiqaq because the Prophet did, crowds prostrating with the Prophet lacked room, and Umar taught that the prostration is right but not compulsory.
Asked about prostrating at Surat Sad, Ibn Abbas cites the verse telling the Prophet to follow David, Solomon and earlier prophets; it is not compulsory, though the Prophet prostrated.
Asked whether Surat Sad has a prostration, Ibn Abbas said yes, since David is among the prophets whose guidance the Prophet was ordered to follow.
Ibn Abbas prostrates in Surat Sad because the Prophet was told to follow the guidance of prophets such as David, who prostrated.
The Prophet prostrated on finishing Surat an-Najm and all with him prostrated, Muslims, pagans, jinn and humans, except Umaiya bin Khalaf, who prostrated on a handful of dust.
